resolutions.researcher_notes: Recovered the KNOWN GOTCHA OPEC ASB2012 PDF via Wayback (live opec.org link dead, redirects home). Downloaded the capture directly with curl and ran `pdftotext -layout`: Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, p.75, contains the exact named row 'Waha/Nasser | Waha | 110 [mi] | 24 [in] | 5,664,118 [1,000 scm/yr] | na' -- this pipeline is individually listed by name as extant transport infrastructure in 2011 (not proposed/planned), directly supporting Status=operating. Second, independent, much more recent source: Waha Oil Company's own English-language site (Wayback snapshot 2025-05-08, content current through Dec 2023 news items) states under 'Waha Oil Company Activities' that natural-gas extraction (استخراج الغاز الطبيعي) is ongoing/in-progress (تحت التنفيذ), and that the company currently operates 373 km of gas transport lines and 10 gas-processing stations company-wide. url_verifier's substring check can't confirm the status token literally (status is inferable, not literal, per the tooling notes), but the page's plain-language description of live, ongoing gas transport operations independently confirms Waha Oil is still running gas pipeline infrastructure 12+ years after the OPEC snapshot. Two independent origins (OPEC statistical body, 2011; Waha Oil's own corporate site, 2023-2025) spanning over a decade -- tier high.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012 (see Status notes), Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' -- the 'Waha/Nasser' row sits specifically in the gas-pipeline table (distinct from Table 4.11's petroleum-product-pipeline roster a few pages later), making Fuel=Gas definitional to the table it appears in. Second source: Waha Oil Company's own English site (Wayback 2025-05-08) lists 'Natural Gas Extraction' as one of only three core company activities (crude production, crude exploration, natural gas extraction) alongside '10 gas processing stations' and '373 km gas transport lines' company-wide -- confirms Waha Oil transports gas as a matter of course, though this source doesn't name the Waha/Nasser line specifically. Two independent origins but the second is company-level rather than pipeline-specific, so tier medium rather than high.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, row 'Waha/Nasser | Waha': Capacity column = 5,664,118 (units: 1,000 scm/yr per the table's column header) = 5,664,118,000 scm/yr = 5.664 bcm/y -- matches the sheet's value ('5.66' bcm/y) to 3 significant figures exactly. Single source; no independent second source found stating this specific pipeline's capacity (Waha Oil's own site gives only an aggregate company-wide gas-transport-line length, not a per-line capacity figure). tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Waha/Nasser | Waha' row: Length = 110 miles = 177.03 km (110 x 1.609344) -- matches the sheet's LengthKnown value ('177.00' km) essentially exactly (rounding only). Single source; Waha Oil's own site gives only an aggregate 373 km of gas transport lines company-wide, not a broken-out per-line length, so it doesn't independently corroborate this specific 177 km figure. tier medium.

Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Waha/Nasser | Waha' row: Diameter column = 24 (inches) -- exact match to the sheet's value ('24.00', DiameterUnits='in'). Single source; no independent second source found stating this specific pipeline's diameter. tier medium.

Country-level value only (Start/EndCountryOrArea = Libya, no sub-national endpoints given in the brief). Two independent sources agree: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists 'Waha/Nasser' under the 'Libya' section header alongside the other Sirte Basin lines. (2) Waha Oil Company's own site (Wayback 2025-05-08) gives GPS coordinates for its operated fields (Waha field, Samah field, Gialo field, Zahra field, Faregh field, Sidra port) that place them all within Libya, and states the company's headquarters is in Tripoli, Libya. Two independent origins (OPEC statistics body vs. the operating company's own site) -- tier high, though this is a low-information/undisputed fact.

Operator='Waha Oil Co' confirmed by three independent sources: (1) recovered Wayback ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists Owner/operator='Waha' for the exact 'Waha/Nasser' row (2011 data). (2) NOC's own official affiliated-companies page (noc.ly, verified live) lists 'Waha Oil Company' (Arabic: شركة الواحة للنفط) as an NOC-subsidiary operating company -- confirms both the Operator value and, verbatim, the OperatorLocalLanguage value in the brief. (3) Waha Oil Company's own English site (Wayback 2025-05-08) self-identifies as 'Waha Oil Company' operating the Waha/Samah/Gialo/Zahra/Faregh fields and associated gas/oil transport lines. Three genuinely independent origins (OPEC statistics body, NOC's own corporate listing, and Waha Oil's own site) -- tier high.

Waha Oil Company's own official 'About' page (Arabic; Wayback snapshot 2019-08-20, and this text is stable across every re-crawl I checked through 2024) states the exact structural ownership split resulting from the 1974 nationalization agreement: National Oil Corporation 59.1667%, Continental Oil Co. 16.3333%, Marathon Libya Oil Co. 16.333%, Amerada Libya Oil Co. 8.1667% -- these are the direct historical/legal predecessors of the brief's Owner1-4 (Continental -> ConocoPhillips via 2002 merger; Amerada -> Hess Corp via 2006 rename) and the percentages match the brief's 59.18/16.33/16.33/8.16 to within 0.01 point (rounding only). CONTRADICTION/STALENESS TO FLAG: (a) Marathon, not TotalEnergies, is the entity named in this 2019 (and even 2021-2024) snapshot of Waha Oil's own site -- Wikipedia's Marathon Oil page (verified live, contains 'Libya' and 'TotalEnergies') independently confirms Marathon divested its Libyan assets to TotalEnergies SE in March 2018 for $450M, which is why the brief's Owner3 is correctly 'TotalEnergies SE' even though Waha Oil's own descriptive text hadn't been updated to reflect the buyer's new name as of these snapshots (a company legacy-text lag, not an error in the brief). (b) More significantly, Waha Oil's OWN SITE has since moved on again: a 2025-05-08 snapshot of the same About page states the 'current' participation is now only three-way -- NOC 59.1667%, ConocoPhillips 20.41665%, Total 20.41665% -- with Hess Corp's 8.16% stake fully absorbed by the other two IOC partners since. So the brief's 4-owner split (with Hess Corp still holding 8.16%) reflects a real ownership structure that held from 2018 (Marathon->Total) until some point before mid-2025 (Hess exit) -- it is well-supported historically but is superseded by more current company disclosure; flagging for Baird/QC rather than silently updating to the newer 3-way split, since the brief's ask was to source the value as given. tier medium (exact percentage match, two independent origins, but requires chaining across snapshots/sources rather than one document stating the full modern-name roster directly).
